findings.finding: The expected re-measurement does not follow from the plan's own reproduction. In the original shim run, the 7 stalled calls match exactly one pass of the sweep: `_gc_config_unit` (get gc.auto, which returns 124 and so skips the unset; then get/set gc.autoDetach and get/set maintenance.autoDetach, 5 calls) plus `_merge_ours_unit` (get/set, 2 calls). That means the bootstrap pin at `repo` was not stalled by the shim. If it had been, the run would show 12 calls. So after the fix the shim should show 1 stalled call, not '2 (bootstrap pin + sweep)'. If instead the shim does stall tracker config calls, then init.py's own `_ensure_branch_user_config` and gpgsign calls would also have stalled and would still stall after the fix. In both readings, the plan's model of which calls the fix removes does not match the code paths.
findings.location: Testing — 'Measurement re-run' bullet; Findings — shim reproduction
scenarios: An implementer runs the measurement, gets 1 (or more than 2) stalled calls, and either cannot tell whether the fix works or changes the shim to produce the expected number

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the up-to-30 s _store_git_op_lock acquisition wait (_STORE_GIT_LOCK_WAIT_S) to the stated per-call worst case (≈160 s) and to the theoretical ceiling.
evidence: Plan: 'So a stalled `git config` costs one bound: `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT` (120 s) plus at most 10 s of process-group reaping … 130 s in all.'
src/rebar/_store/git_locking.py:438 `with _store_git_op_lock(tracker):` wraps every attempt of _with_index_lock_retry
src/rebar/_store/git_locking.py:171 `_STORE_GIT_LOCK_WAIT_S = 30.0`; lines 209-225 poll until the deadline, then continue without the lock
findings.finding: The stated worst-case wall time of one run_git_write call is incomplete. _with_index_lock_retry first takes the per-store advisory git-op lock (_store_git_op_lock). When that lock is contended, it polls for up to _STORE_GIT_LOCK_WAIT_S = 30 s before running git. One stalled call can therefore take 120 + 10 + 30 = 160 s, not 130 s, and the theoretical ceiling is about 30 s higher than stated.
findings.location: Findings bullet 1 / Acceptance Criteria line 1 ('worst-case wall time … is measured and stated')
scenarios: Under concurrent verify runs or a sibling rebar process holding rebar-git-op.lock for the same tracker, each config call waits up to 30 s before its 120 s bound starts.
findings.suggested_fix: State the per-call worst case as up to 30 s advisory-lock wait + 120 s bound + 10 s reaping = 160 s, and recompute the retry ceiling the same way (the lock is taken once per run_git_write, outside the retries).

findings.finding: The claim that '7 x 120 s = 840 s … matches the observed 300 s expiry inside `_gc_config_unit` and `_merge_ours_unit`' does not fit the gw2 stack. If every config call stalled for the full 120 s bound, gc-config's 5 calls alone (600 s) would have hit the 300 s timeout inside `_gc_config_unit`. That worker could not have reached `_merge_ours_unit` line 84. Reaching line 84 within 300 s means at most two earlier calls (including the bootstrap pin) took a full bound, so the stall was intermittent rather than every config call. The diagnosis that 'the 300 s went across several sequential bounded calls', with every call stalling, is not supported for gw2.
findings.location: Findings bullets 2-3 ('which matches the observed 300 s expiry inside `_gc_config_unit` and `_merge_ours_unit`')
scenarios: The real stall pattern is intermittent: some calls stall for the full bound and others complete. Stopping at the first timeout then also skips units that would have converged, and the root-cause narrative recorded for AC2 is wrong.

findings.finding: The acceptance criteria are generic ('A fix ... lands, with a regression test if a code defect is found') and do not state the observable outcomes the plan commits to. Uncovered outcomes: the sweep stops after the first timed-out call; skipped units are recorded `failed` and kept out of `.ensure-applied`; init never aborts and logs a warning; no unit reports `changed` on a timeout. The described deliverables therefore have no covering criterion, and AC3 can be ticked by any fix.

findings.finding: AC2 asks that the blocked-`git config` condition be 'reproduced', but the plan reproduces only the timeout amplification, using a shim that injects the stall. It also states that what stalled git is not established. The AC does not say whether a simulated stall counts as reproduction, and the shim experiment has no recorded location or proving command for re-running it.

findings.finding: Making the `_init_ensures._git` seam raise `EnsureGitTimeout` changes the contract of every unit function (`_gc_config_unit`, `_merge_ours_unit`, ...) for every caller, not only `run_ensures`. The plan names one direct caller outside the sweep, the init bootstrap pin, and wraps it. It does not state that the unit functions have been enumerated for other direct callers, such as doctor/repair commands, migrations or write-path ensure hooks. Any such caller would now see an uncaught exception where it previously got a (false) success.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a failure-disposition statement: `EnsureGitTimeout` is transient/retryable, and state what `rebar init` and sweep-triggering writes surface (exit code, message) when the sweep halts on it, as distinct from a permanent unit failure
evidence: Plan: 'records that unit `failed` with the timeout message, records every later unit `failed` with "skipped: <unit> git timed out"'
Plan: 'Failed units stay out of `.ensure-applied`, so the next write's pending hint and the next sweep retry them'
Absence: no 'transient'/'retryable' vs 'permanent' wording, and no stated exit code or user-visible outcome for `rebar init` or for a write whose sweep halts
findings.finding: The plan adds a new exception arm (`EnsureGitTimeout`) and changes what the sweep surfaces (units `failed`, sweep halted). It does not state the disposition with an explicit word, or what the end caller sees. Is a git-watchdog timeout classed as transient/retryable (implied only by 'the next sweep retry them')? What exit status and message does `rebar init`, or a write that triggers a sweep, return when the sweep reports these `failed` units: success with a warning, or a failure exit? Is that different from how a genuinely failing (permanent) unit is surfaced?
findings.location: Approach step 1 (`run_ensures` stops the sweep on `EnsureGitTimeout`)
scenarios: `rebar init` on a stalled filesystem: the user cannot tell from the plan whether init exits 0 with ensures pending, or non-zero.
A write triggers a sweep that halts: the caller cannot tell whether to retry later or treat the result as an error.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a line such as: 'Failure-disposition contract: a git watchdog timeout in an ensure is transient/retryable — `run_ensures` records the unit and all later units `failed` (excluded from `.ensure-applied`, retried on the next sweep); `rebar init` and writes still exit 0 and log a warning naming the pending units; a non-timeout unit error keeps its existing disposition.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State and resolve the consequence of stopping the sweep: after a single transient timeout, gitignore, gitattributes and store-compat are skipped on a fresh store while push.py uses `add -A`. Either show the risk is acceptable or limit the damage, e.g. run the units that protect commits before the git-config units, or skip only units that use the git seam that timed out.
evidence: Plan: "records every later unit `failed` with \"skipped: <unit> git timed out\", and runs no further unit"

Plan: "Failed units stay out of `.ensure-applied`, so the next write's pending hint and the next sweep retry them". The hint (`maybe_emit_pending_hint`) only logs a warning, and a sweep runs only from init or fsck --repair
ensures.py:63-74 REGISTRY_IDS order: env-id, gc-config, merge-ours, gitattributes, gitignore, store-compat, ...
push.py:421: `staged = _git(canonical, "add", "-A")` stages everything in the store
_init_ensures.py:22-38 `_GITIGNORE` lists .env-id, .write.lock, .cache.json, .state-cache and other runtime artifacts
findings.finding: Stopping the whole sweep at the first timeout turns one transient stall into skipping every later unit. Those include the units that protect commits: gitattributes, gitignore and store-compat. On a fresh store this leaves no committed .gitignore. Only re-init or `rebar store fsck --repair` re-runs the sweep; the write path only logs a rate-limited hint. Meanwhile push.py stages the store with `git add -A`, so runtime artifacts that .gitignore is meant to exclude (.env-id, .write.lock, .cache.json, .state-cache) can be committed. Today a transient stall in gc-config only delays the later units, which then converge. The plan does not discuss this trade-off.
findings.location: Approach step 1 (run_ensures stops the sweep) / REGISTRY_IDS ordering in src/rebar/_store/ensures.py
scenarios: Fresh init on a loaded host: one gc-config `config --get` hits the 120 s bound once, then the filesystem recovers. gitignore, gitattributes and store-compat are skipped, and the next ticket write's `add -A` commits runtime files to the tickets branch
The same transient stall on re-init of an older store: missing .gitignore lines are not added until someone runs fsck --repair
